subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the centroid of the tetrahedron whose vertices are (2, 3, −4), (−3, 3, 2), (−1, 4, 2) and (3, 5, 1).

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what the centroid of a tetrahedron is in terms of its vertices, and what number you divide by.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the centroid formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. A tetrahedron has four vertices, so its centroid is the average of four points. The formula is the triangle one with a fourth term and a 4 underneath.
steps.memory_tip: A tetrahedron has FOUR vertices, so the centroid divides by 4, not 3.

recall.must_convey: That the centroid of a tetrahedron is the average of its four vertices, one coordinate at a time.
accept: the centroid of a tetrahedron is the average of the four vertices
add the four x values and divide by four, same for y and z
it is the triangle formula with a fourth term and four underneath
tetrahedron ki naalugu vertices, kabatti four tho divide cheyyali
write the four vertex centroid formula
reject: divide by three because it is a centroid

steps.why: The divisor is the number of vertices being averaged, so it changes from 3 to 4 when the figure changes from a triangle to a tetrahedron. Nothing else in the formula changes.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 3, which is the triangle formula.
Leaving out one of the four vertices while adding a column.

steps.label: Work out the three averages
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Take one column at a time. Two of the four x values and one of the z values are negative, so add the signed numbers carefully.
steps.memory_tip: Do one column at a time. The x and z columns both come to 1, so both give 1/4.

recall.must_convey: That the three column averages give the centroid (1/4, 15/4, 1/4).
accept: the x column adds to one so the x coordinate is one by four
the y column adds to fifteen so it is fifteen by four
the centroid is one by four, fifteen by four, one by four
prathi column separate ga add chesi four tho divide cheyyali
reject: the centroid of a tetrahedron is the average of the four vertices

steps.why: Each coordinate of the centroid depends only on the matching coordinates of the vertices, so the three columns are three separate additions and a slip in one does not spread to the others.
common_mistakes: Reading −3 as +3 in the x column.
Dividing the coordinate sums by 3 instead of 4; a tetrahedron has four vertices.
